title: Failure Mode Playbook — scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick, informal playbook sketch for classifying and mitigating failure modes in the inference path (hosted / dedicated / private).

Context notes (quick):
- We have multiple failure domains: model-accuracy regressions, latency spikes, hardware OOMs, KV cache corruption/staleness, quota overrun, third-party infra (network/storage) outages, and billing/authorization errors.
- Current runbooks exist in SRE but are either too infra-focused or too high-level. Product teams need a digestible set of mitigation flows that map straight to toggles/routes in Console and SDK.

Goals for this doc:
- Define common failure classes and signal-to-action mappings (what to watch, when to fire a mitigation).
- Provide compact user stories + acceptance criteria for building playbook UI + APIs.
- Capture quick remediation steps that non-SRE engineers can use during incidents.
- Outline experiments / canary policies to test automated fallback behaviors.

Audience: on-call SREs, runtime engineers, solutions eng, CS for enterprise customers, and product owners for rollback/fallback features.

High level failure classes (initial taxonomy):
1) Quality regression: sudden drop in response relevance or hallucination rate for a model or customer prompt set.
2) Latency degradation: p95/p99 increases beyond SLA without load increase.
3) Capacity exhaustion: queued requests grow, GPUs saturated, autoscaler not responding.
4) Cache inconsistency: KV cache returning stale context or causing response corruption.
5) Cost spike / billing anomaly: per-token or infrastructure cost jumps unexpectedly.
6) Authorization / configuration drift: keys revoked, route misconfiguration, model unpinned.
7) Hardware failure: GPU process crash, node down, model not loading.
8) External dependency failure: cloud storage / network cross-region issues.

For each class we want: what signals, quick triage, automatic mitigations (if any), and manual actions.

Example: Quality regression (sketch)
- Signals: sharp increase in user-reported low-quality flags; eval metric regression on prod prompt set; increase in rerank skips; auto-evals downgrade > 5% in 30m.
- Quick triage: check model version rollout windows, inspect recent deploys, run canned evals against golden prompt set, look for quantization/compilation changes.
- Auto-mitigations (proposed): immediate traffic split away from suspect model -> fallback to previous pinned version (route-level toggle). Postpone batching/quantization optimizations for affected routes.
- Manual actions: rollback model variant, open PR to revert faulty compilation flags, notify CS and customer if customer-specific model.

Latency degradation (sketch)
- Signals: p95/p99 delta > 2x baseline, queue depth > threshold, GPU utilization > 90% across pool, spike in kernel time.
- Quick triage: correlate to traffic surge vs config change; check autoscaler events, check kernel swap logs, inspect recent batch size/timeout changes.
- Auto-mitigations: switch to lower-latency model variant (smaller model / quantized), enable synchronous mode with shorter timeouts, route to different region or Dedicated pool.
- Manual: increase capacity commit temporarily (if Dedicated), apply emergency burst capacity, reduce token_limit for long-running requests.

KV cache inconsistency (sketch)
- Signals: sudden increase in weird repeats, context mismatches, user complaints about missing prior context; cache eviction errors in logs; cache health metrics show negative hit-rate.
- Triage: determine whether cache invalidation job ran, check redis/memcached errors, inspect session keys and TTLs, check for new serialization changes.
- Auto: switch to stateless mode for affected sessions (fall back to prefix-only context), flush and rebuild KV shards progressively, disable cross-session stitching.
- Manual: run targeted cache flush for specific tenant, replay warmup for sessions, rehydrate cache from snapshots.

User stories (to scope product features)
- As an SRE, I want a single-pane playbook card for each failure class with one-click mitigations so I can act fast during incidents.
- As a platform engineer, I want programmatic APIs to trigger route-level fallbacks and pin model versions so recovery can be automated by other orchestrations.
- As a solutions engineer, I want per-customer diagnostics (recent deploys, evals, tokens) surfaced so I can advise an enterprise during an outage.
- As a product owner, I want experiments to validate automated fallback correctness before enabling them in prod.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Playbook UI card exists for 4 failure classes (quality, latency, capacity, cache). Each card shows signals, triage checklist, and 2 actionable mitigations (at least one reversible).
- APIs to programmatically split traffic and pin/unpin model versions with audit logs.
- Canary experiment runner: rollouts can auto-switch to fallback for 5% of traffic and record eval checks.
- Alerts map to playbook cards with links to runbook steps and suggested mitigations.

Monitoring signals to add / refine (quick list):
- eval_regression_rate (per-route, 1m/5m/1h), user_quality_flags, auto_eval_score_drop, p95_latency_route, queue_depth_route, gpu_util_pool, kv_hit_rate_tenant, cache_error_rate, billing_spike_detected, config_change_event, model_load_failures.

Minimal UI flows (notes):
- One-click: pin previous model -> confirm -> system rolls 100% of route to pinned version (with audit and optional customer notification template).
- Traffic split slider: 0-100, can set duration, health-check threshold to auto-revert.
- Dry-run mode: simulate automated fallback (no traffic change) and run evals to estimate quality impact.

Safety & guardrails (must have)
- Any automated fallback must be gated by a dry-run + canary phase (5% then 20%) and have automatic rollback if evals/retries worsen.
- Rate-limit automated mitigations per-customer (avoid flip-flopping).
- Audit trail + pre-filled incident template to notify customers for enterprise plans.

Experiment ideas (short):
- Chaos test: deliberately corrupt a KV shard in staging, run the auto-mitigations, measure recovery time and user-visible degradation.
- Latency fallback A/B: compare lower-capacity quantized variant vs original for quality/latency tradeoffs across controlled traffic.
- Cost-aware fallback: automatically route to cheaper variant when cost-per-token > threshold while bounding quality drop.

Open questions / TODOs (brain dump):
- How to handle multi-tenant caches where flush for one tenant may impact others? Need per-tenant shard mapping and soft-evict API.
- Who owns the customer communication templates? CS or legal? Need standard SLO language for fallbacks.
- Metrics: what is the golden eval set per-route? Where does it live and who maintains it?
- Latency mitigation that routes to different regions: security/data residency implications for Private deployments.

Next immediate steps (short):
- Sync with SRE and Console PMs (Mira + product) to surface playbook card prototypes and validate API contract (week of Mar 3).
- Implement basic alerts->playbook mapping for quality and latency (prototype parser + UI link).
- Build small canary runner that flips route to pinned model for 5% and runs auto-evals.

Notes to self (casual):
- Keep playbook language short and action-oriented; SREs want checklists not essays.
- Prioritize reversible actions first (traffic split, pin/unpin) and have a clear rollback path for irreversible ones.
- Surface customer-impact estimation for each mitigation (cost & quality).

Quick checklist:
- [ ] Draft UI mockups for playbook card
- [ ] Define API contract for pin/split/dryrun
- [ ] Create sample incident email template
- [ ] Add auto-eval configs to CI for canary runner

End of sketch.

(Notes intentionally rough; will clean up after initial sync.)
